transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I can handle the technical parts of my job fine, but I just can’t seem to keep all the pieces of these projects organized anymore. Ever since I was promoted to lead architect about a year ago, the sheer volume of moving parts has become really difficult to manage.
Do you find that this difficulty with organization and focus has been a lifelong struggle for you, or is it something that only started when your workload increased a year ago?

It definitely became much more disruptive after I took on this new role a year ago, but looking back, it's actually a lifelong struggle. Even in primary school, my report cards always said "brilliant ideas but careless mistakes," and my parents had to sit with me just to keep me focused on my homework. So the roots have always been there, but I used to be able to mask them better.
Beyond the struggles with organization and focus, have you been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in the things you used to enjoy over this past year?

No, I haven't been feeling persistently sad or hopeless, and I haven't lost interest in my hobbies like sketching or reading sci-fi. It's more that I find it very difficult to sit quietly and actually focus on them lately because of this constant restless feeling.

When you experience this constant restless feeling, is it primarily driven by excessive worry about your work performance and potential future consequences, or is it more of a physical need to be moving and doing something else?

It’s definitely more of a physical sensation than cognitive worry. I feel this restless buzz in my body that makes me feel stuck, so I constantly shift in my chair, pace around, or fidget with my hands just to burn off that energy. It is especially noticeable during long Zoom calls or when I'm trying to sit quietly.
